name: Exact Component-Label Criterion for a Three-Vertex Path Reduction
statement: Let $A$ be corner-peelable ample, let $D=\{u,c,v\}$ induce a path, and lift each component $K_i$ of $A\setminus D$ to layer $t_i$. The resulting ample expansion $X_t$ is corner-peelable exactly when some acyclic USO $\mathcal O$ of $A$ and some endpoint $z\in\{u,v\}$ make the labels on $N_{\mathcal O}(z)$ constant (with empty and singleton sets allowed). Equivalently, the nonpeelable labelings are precisely the proper two-colourings of every edge of $\mathcal H(A,D)$.
proof: Given such an orientation and endpoint, first delete vertices outside the set reachable from $D$; those exclusive deletions lift. All surviving external neighbours of the selected endpoint then have one label, so its opposite lift is a corner. The remaining reduction is an edge convex in the contraction and hence peels. Conversely, in any peeling of the expansion, the first deletion over $D$ must occur at an endpoint. Earlier exclusive deletions project to a contraction prefix, which can be completed to an acyclic USO; vertices reachable from $D$ survive that prefix, and the corner test forces the relevant surviving component labels to be constant.
